sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: Along the estuaries of Goa lie the khazans, low-lying lands reclaimed from tidal waters many centuries ago. Their builders had no machines, yet they solved a problem that still troubles coastal engineers: how to keep salt water out of a field without cutting the field off from the river. The answer was a chain of earthen embankments, called bunds, broken at intervals by wooden sluice gates. At high tide the pressure of the river pushes each gate shut; when the tide falls, the gate swings open and lets rainwater drain away. No one needs to stand guard.

What made the system last, however, was not the carpentry but the arrangement around it. Village associations auctioned the right to catch fish at the sluice gates, and the money paid for repairs to the bunds. A farmer who grew rice behind an embankment therefore depended on the fisherman who leased the gate, and the fisherman on the farmer. Neglect by either was soon noticed by the other.

That balance has weakened. As younger people have left farming, many fields lie fallow, and a bund that protects nothing valuable is seldom repaired. When a breach is left open through a monsoon, the salt that enters can take years to wash out. Some observers treat the khazans as a relic. Others point out that a rising sea makes a working, low-cost tidal defence more useful, not less, and that reviving it would cost a fraction of building concrete walls.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: When a government office moves a service online, the usual measure of success is the number of applications received through the portal. The figure is easy to collect and usually flattering. It says little, however, about the people who never applied.

Consider a certificate that once required two visits to a taluka office. Online, it can be requested at midnight from a phone. For a salaried applicant in a town this is a clear gain. For an elderly widow in a hill village, the same change may mean paying a cyber-cafe operator to fill in a form she cannot read, on a connection that fails twice before the document uploads. Her cost has not disappeared; it has moved from the bus fare to the intermediary. The office, meanwhile, records one more successful online application.

None of this is an argument for returning to the counter and the queue. Digital delivery removes many small opportunities for delay and for the demand of a bribe, and it leaves a record of when each file was opened and by whom. The point is narrower. A service should be judged by whether those who are entitled to it actually receive it, and at what cost to them, rather than by how many transactions the system logs. Offices that keep an assisted counter open alongside the portal, and that count rejected and abandoned applications as carefully as approved ones, tend to learn where their design is failing. Those that count only successes learn nothing they did not already wish to believe.

questions.q: According to the passage, what closes a sluice gate at high tide?
opts: A villager posted at the embankment
The pressure of the river water
The weight of the fish caught at the gate
questions.why: Paragraph 1 says that at high tide the pressure of the river pushes each gate shut.

questions.q: As used in the last paragraph, the word "relic" most nearly means:
opts: something left over from the past that has outlived its use
questions.why: The word is set against the view that the khazans are still useful, so it means a leftover that no longer serves a purpose.

questions.q: The author says the khazan system lasted mainly because:
opts: the gates were made of durable wood
farmers and gate lessees depended on each other, and fishing revenue paid for repairs
the sea level stayed the same for centuries
questions.why: Paragraph 2 credits the arrangement around the gates, not the carpentry: fishing rights funded repairs and each party watched the other.

questions.q: Which of the following can be inferred from the third paragraph?
opts: A bund is less likely to be repaired when the fields behind it are not cultivated
Salt that enters a field is washed out within one monsoon
Younger people have deliberately damaged the bunds
Fallow fields are better protected than cultivated ones
questions.why: Fields lie fallow, and a bund that protects nothing valuable is seldom repaired. The passage says salt can take years to wash out.

questions.q: Those who favour reviving the khazans argue chiefly that:
opts: a rising sea makes a cheap, working tidal defence more useful
concrete walls cannot be built in Goa
rice grown in khazans fetches a higher price
questions.why: The last sentence gives their case: a rising sea makes a low-cost tidal defence more useful, and revival costs far less than concrete walls.

questions.q: The central idea of the passage is that:
opts: online services should be withdrawn from villages
the number of online applications does not show whether a service reaches everyone entitled to it
government offices should stop collecting data
questions.why: The author wants a service judged by whether entitled people receive it and at what cost, not by the count of transactions.

questions.q: The example of the elderly widow is used to show that:
opts: rural citizens are opposed to technology
certificates should be delivered at home
the cost of obtaining a service can shift to a new form without disappearing
questions.why: Her cost has not disappeared; it has moved from the bus fare to the intermediary.

questions.q: Which benefit of digital delivery does the author acknowledge?
opts: It reduces openings for delay and bribe demands, and records who handled a file
It guarantees that every application is approved
It improves internet connections in remote areas
questions.why: Paragraph 3 says digital delivery removes opportunities for delay and bribes and leaves a record of when each file was opened and by whom.

questions.q: By calling the figure "usually flattering", the author suggests that it:
opts: tends to make the office look more successful than a fuller picture would
understates the work done by staff
questions.why: The figure is accurate but leaves out those who never applied, so it shows the office in a better light than the whole picture.

questions.q: According to the last paragraph, an office is more likely to discover faults in its design if it:
opts: closes its counter and relies on the portal alone
publishes only the number of approved applications
keeps an assisted counter open and counts rejected and abandoned applications
raises the fee for online applications
questions.why: Such offices "tend to learn where their design is failing".

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Neither the Collector nor the Mamlatdars ______ present at yesterday's hearing.
questions.why: With neither ... nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject. "Mamlatdars" is plural and "yesterday" needs the past tense.

questions.q: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
opts: She is senior than me in service.
She is more senior than me in service.
She is senior to me in service.
She is senior from me in service.
questions.why: Senior, junior, superior, inferior and prior take "to", not "than", and are not used with "more".

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: The officer said to the applicant, "Have you brought your documents?"
opts: The officer asked the applicant whether he had brought his documents.
The officer asked the applicant whether had he brought his documents.
The officer told the applicant that he has brought his documents.
The officer asked the applicant if you have brought your documents.
questions.why: A yes/no question is reported with if or whether, in statement word order, with the present perfect shifted to the past perfect and the pronouns changed.

questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: The clerk is verifying the land records.
opts: The land records were being verified by the clerk.
The land records have been verified by the clerk.
The land records are verified by the clerk.
The land records are being verified by the clerk.
questions.why: Present continuous active (is verifying) becomes is/are being + past participle.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: If I ______ the notice earlier, I would have applied in time.
questions.why: A third conditional about an unreal past uses if + past perfect, then would have + past participle.

questions.q: The headquarters of Kushavati, the third district of Goa notified on 31 December 2025, is at:
questions.why: Kushavati was carved out of South Goa with Quepem, Sanguem, Dharbandora and Canacona talukas. Its headquarters is Quepem.

questions.q: On its 39th Statehood Day (30 May 2025), Goa was declared fully literate under which programme?
questions.why: The declaration was made under ULLAS (New India Literacy Programme), which treats 95% literacy as full literacy.

questions.q: Who assumed office as the Governor of Goa on 26 July 2025?
questions.why: Ashok Gajapathi Raju, a former Union Civil Aviation Minister, succeeded P. S. Sreedharan Pillai.

questions.q: The FIDE World Cup 2025, held in Goa, was won by:
questions.why: Javokhir Sindarov of Uzbekistan beat Wei Yi in the tie-breaks on 26 November 2025 and became the youngest World Cup winner.

questions.q: India won the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2026 by defeating which team in the final at Ahmedabad?
questions.why: India beat New Zealand by 96 runs on 8 March 2026 at the Narendra Modi Stadium for a third T20 World Cup title.

questions.q: On attaining statehood on 30 May 1987, Goa became which state of the Indian Union?
questions.why: Goa became the 25th state. Daman and Diu remained a Union Territory.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions?
questions.why: The 73rd Amendment (1992) added Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule. The 74th deals with municipalities.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India lays down the functions of Public Service Commissions?
questions.why: Article 320 sets out the functions. Article 315 provides for the Commissions and Article 316 for the appointment of members.

questions.q: The Goa Opinion Poll, in which voters rejected merger with Maharashtra, was held in:
questions.why: The Opinion Poll was held on 16 January 1967. The date is observed in Goa as Asmitai Dis.

questions.q: Konkani was added to the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution by which Amendment?
questions.why: The 71st Amendment (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali. The 56th Amendment gave Goa statehood.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 7, 10, 16, 28, 52, ?
questions.why: The differences double each time: 3, 6, 12, 24, then 48. So 52 + 48 = 100.

questions.q: If MARGAO is written as NBSHBP in a certain code, how is PANAJI written in that code?
questions.why: Each letter moves one place forward: P-Q, A-B, N-O, A-B, J-K, I-J.

questions.q: D and E are a married couple, and D is the husband. A and B are their children. A is B's brother, and B is the mother of C. How is C related to E?
questions.why: E is the mother of B, and B is the mother of C, so C is E's grandchild. Nothing in the statement tells us whether C is male or female.

questions.q: Ramesh walks 9 km towards the north, turns right and walks 12 km. How far is he from his starting point in a straight line?
questions.why: The two legs are at right angles, so the distance is the hypotenuse: the square root of 81 + 144 = 225, which is 15 km.

questions.q: Statements: All files are records. Some records are confidential documents. Conclusions: I. Some files are confidential documents. II. Some confidential documents are records.
questions.why: II is the second statement turned around, so it follows. I does not: the confidential records need not be files.

questions.q: Five officers P, Q, R, S and T sit in a row facing north. R sits exactly in the middle. P sits to the immediate left of R. T does not sit at either end. Q does not sit next to P. Who sits at the extreme right end?
questions.why: R is third and P second. T is not at an end, so T is fourth. Q cannot sit next to P, so Q is fifth and S is first. The order is S, P, R, T, Q.

questions.q: In a row of 40 candidates, Meena is 14th from the left end. What is her position from the right end?
questions.why: Position from the right = total - position from the left + 1 = 40 - 14 + 1 = 27.

questions.q: Find the odd one out.
questions.why: Mandovi, Zuari and Chapora are rivers of Goa. Dudhsagar is a waterfall.

questions.q: 1 January 2026 was a Thursday. What day of the week was 1 March 2026?
questions.why: January has 31 days and February 2026 has 28, a gap of 59 days. 59 leaves a remainder of 3 when divided by 7, and three days after Thursday is Sunday.

questions.q: The present ages of a father and his son are in the ratio 7 : 2. Five years from now the ratio will be 8 : 3. What is the father's present age?
questions.why: Let the ages be 7x and 2x. Then 3(7x + 5) = 8(2x + 5), so x = 5 and the father is 35. That is not among options A to D.
